translation_notes: EXCLUDED (AGENT_BATCH case for this batch, path contains _vendor_): this file is a verbatim vendored copy of rdflib's own test suite, not application code written against rdflib. Checked against rdflib 7.2.1's sdist (test/test_having.py, downloaded and diffed): the module-level fixture (`g = Graph()` plus a `data = """..."""` Turtle string parsed with `g.parse(data=data, format="turtle")`) and all three test functions (test_group_by, test_having_aggregate_eq_literal, test_having_primary_expression_var_neq_iri) are byte-for-byte identical to upstream rdflib. Blackcat-Informatics/purrdf vendored the whole rdflib_suite under bindings/python/tests/rdflib_suite/vendor/ to exercise their own bindings against rdflib's reference behaviour. Translating this region would credit ldpy with rewriting rdflib's own test suite rather than code written by an application against rdflib -- exactly the case the brief says to classify excluded and leave untranslated rather than force.

Left untranslated (translated.ldpy is the mechanical draft, identical to original.py). Not run through rdfeval check: the extracted region also drops the module-level `data = ...; g.parse(data=data, format="turtle")` statement that populates `g` in the real file (only in the surrounding, non-extracted lines), so `g.query(query)` on the bare `g = Graph()` shown here would in fact return 0 rows, not the 2 the assertion expects -- a further sign this region needs its enclosing test module, not a standalone extraction, to mean anything.
